blogs.title: The First Five Days: Preoperative Heparin and Early-Onset HIT in Cardiac Surgery
blogs.description: This post explores the often-overlooked risk of early heparin exposure during preoperative catheterization leading to HIT symptoms before the classic postoperative window. We discuss how to modify the algorithm for thrombocytopenia when platelet counts begin dropping within the first postoperative day, distinguishing pre-antigenic exposure from typical CPB-associated latency.

blogs.title: The Silent Threat: Autoimmune HIT and the High-Risk of Thrombotic Stroke
blogs.description: A clinical lesson on recognizing Autoimmune HIT (aHIT) versus classic HIT. This entry details the severe phenotypic presentation, including platelet nadirs and arterial thrombosis, highlighting the 'silent threat' where classic prophylactic failure is overtaken by a novel, heparin-independent antibody profile.

blogs.title: Inhibition or Inevitable Activation? Interpreting Atypical Serotonin-Release Assay Profiles in HIT
blogs.description: Moving beyond standard serology, this blog dives deep into the nuanced interpretation of the Serotonin-Release Assay (SRA). We analyze the specific case findings where serotonin release occurred without heparin and exceeded expected Fc-receptor blockade, offering a practical guide for clinicians managing 'indeterminate' HIT serology.

blogs.title: Bringing the Hemorrhage Risk: Choosing Anticoagulants in HIT with Acute Stroke
blogs.description: This post addresses a critical management dilemma: managing a hypercoagulable HIT patient who has sustained a thrombotic stroke. We evaluate the trade-offs between direct thrombin inhibitors (Argatroban) and Factor Xa inhibitors (Fondaparinux) in the setting of acute neurological injury and severe thrombocytopenia.

blogs.title: The IVIG Reality Check: Efficacy and Limitations in Severe Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: A critical review of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) as an adjunctive therapy in severe HIT. Using this case as a reference, we discuss the variability of clinical response, the timing of therapeutic benefit, and the growing evidence regarding IVIG's role in managing aHIT specifically.
